One real request, traced

  1. You run the export command. The tool reads raw/01.png and checks its size and file fingerprint.
  2. The file matches a supplied placeholder. The tool sets ready to false and keeps the actual image as the source.
  3. The page puts that image inside the measured phone opening and adds a DRAFT banner.
  4. Chrome exports the page through html-to-image twice to warm up images and fonts, then saves the second result.
  5. The tool checks 1320 × 2868, removes the PNG alpha channel, and writes the numbered file.

Actual code: what counts as ready

Source: screenshots/export.mjs. A fingerprint means the file's exact content. Known placeholder content stays flagged. A new image must be exactly the planned size to lose its banner. That check cannot tell whether it shows the right screen.

Lines 20–26
    const data = await readFile(new URL(name,raw));
    const {width,height} = await sharp(data).metadata();
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex');
    const suppliedPlaceholder = originalPlaceholders.includes(hash);
    const ready = !suppliedPlaceholder && width===1320 && height===2868;
    await copyFile(new URL(name,raw),new URL(`public/captures/${name}`,import.meta.url));
    captures.push({src:`/captures/${name}`,ready,status:ready?'Full-size capture · content review pending':suppliedPlaceholder?`Supplied placeholder ${name} · replacement capture pending`:`${width} × ${height} · 1320 × 2868 capture pending`});

Actual code: rendering the PNG

Source: screenshots/src/app/page.tsx. decode waits for every image. The first toPng warms up the renderer; the second creates the saved image. finally puts the hidden export copy back even when something fails.

Lines 43–52
async function exportNode(el: HTMLElement) {
  await document.fonts.ready;
  await Promise.all(Array.from(el.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.decode()));
  Object.assign(el.style, {left:'0px', zIndex:'-1', opacity:'1'});
  try {
    const opts = {width:W, height:H, pixelRatio:1, cacheBust:false};
    await toPng(el, opts);
    return await toPng(el, opts);
  } finally { Object.assign(el.style, {left:'-9999px', zIndex:'', opacity:''}); }
}

What was checked

All three icon options: 1024 × 1024, no alpha, no text, square outer edges. Six exports: 1320 × 2868, no alpha. The generator ran in real Chrome and passed TypeScript checking. Real capture 01 and pending capture 04 were visually inspected. The product app was not launched or changed.
